brief: Grass-green index-specimen on warm paper: a reflective standfirst ruled over the work, tomorrow's years first, the original mark standing at the top.
rationale:
The phrase is a forward instruction in the plural — the opportunities of tomorrow — so the page cannot be a single poster line held in isolation; it has to show the opportunities. That pointed me straight to `hero_object: list`: the quote becomes a reflective standfirst and Doug's forward work (dougmar.ch 2026, 15th Club 2025, FishSticks 2025, then the older experiments) reads as a twelve-column index ordered newest-first, so the structure literally spends its attention on what is next. The broken, interrupted twelve-grid lets one row (dougmar.ch, the current year) break its alignment as the focal caesura, which keeps the page from reading as a tidy template.

Spectral + Albert Sans is the chassis because the quote wants a considered, literary register, not a shout, and its quietest-tier display (64→96 hero, 64→120 at 5xl) is exactly the reservation the catalog describes for reflective lines — the quote sits in display italic while the index titles take the 5xl marquee at small caps. It is also fresh against a fourteen-day run that leaned on condensed and grotesque faces. The treatment moves off eight nights of sameness on every field the mandate tracks: small caps (not mixed/lower/caps), italic lead, left alignment (not right/centred/justified), and type-as-texture from the oversized index.

Palette and shell follow. Light-ground on warm green-tinted paper breaks the recent run of drench, dark-void and split-field, and it is the one ground where the Brand Contract actively wants the original green-and-blue mark — so the real stacked-lg mark anchors the top-left masthead in its own colors, which it has effectively never done on the shipped site. One committed grass-green accent at 112° carries the growth reading of "tomorrow" while clearing every forbidden hue zone, and ruled hairlines (`ground_material: rule`) do the specimen's layout work. A left-to-right `wipe` entrance reads as forward motion, and on-scroll reveal brings the index rows up as evidence as you read down.

hero.copy: Spend eighty percent of your time focusing on the opportunities of tomorrow rather than the problems of yesterday.
hero.rationale: This is `signals.quote` (Brian Tracy), and it carries the day because it is a working instruction, not a mood: an 80/20 rule pointed forward, which is exactly how Doug frames his own practice ("Still the vehicle for the next experiment"). Rather than set it as a lone poster, I let it do work it was built for: it becomes the standfirst over Doug's work index, and the forward-leaning projects (dougmar.ch 2026, 15th Club 2025, FishSticks 2025) are the opportunities the line names. Brian Tracy is set as a visible caption under the line. Owner's voice: Doug spends his energy on what ships next, not on relitigating finished work, and he'd read this as plain operating advice, not a slogan.

adBrief.selfCheck:
1. Hero quotability: Yes — a forward-pointed 80/20 instruction, quotable standing alone and attributed.
2. Because-of chain: Yes — forward quote → work-as-evidence list → index-specimen tuple → reflective Spectral → grass-green on paper → ruled twelve-column grid.
3. Render feasibility: Yes — Spectral 5xl reaches 120px; index titles at clamp max 116px fit without overflow, quote standfirst sits at 4xl.
4. Canvas floor feasible: Yes — a full-width ruled index of seven projects plus standfirst and colophon fills 72% comfortably.
5. Phone: Yes — at 360 the reordered quote leads at `2xl` inside the first fold without cutting a word.

adBrief.compositionRationale: I kept the date-derived starting tuple's structural spine (irregular-twelve, vertical, broken, interrupted, none, balanced, reorder) because a reflective instruction paired with evidence wants a ruled index read top to bottom, not a poster. I moved hero_object from `artifact` to `list`: the quote names "opportunities of tomorrow" in the plural, so the forward work (newest years first) leads as a multi-row index, not one piece. I moved hero_zone from `full-bleed` to `edge-bound` so the quote binds to the top edge as a standfirst band over the index, which is how a standfirst-above-list actually sits; full-bleed would have forced the quote to be the whole first screen and starved the object.

colorScheme.color_story: Warm green-tinted paper with one committed grass-green accent reads as growth and next-season, the quote about tomorrow set on a ground that is already greening; the hue sits at 112 because the mandate's 140-180 target falls entirely inside its own 130-252 forbidden band and within 20 degrees of the recently-shipped 160 and 176 greens, so 112 is the nearest growth-green that clears every avoid zone and maximizes distance from the recent window.

shell.footer: colophon block — the day's signals as a ruled typographic index under one strong green rule, no nav

header.nav: No header bar (posture none). The original green-and-blue mark, stacked-lg, sits top-left of the paper index inside the first fold at 1440 and 360. Navigation resolves as Work, About and Contact inside one running small-caps sentence set low under the quote standfirst, accent-green links on paper.

[check 4] The lockup is declared stacked-lg, but no "Doug March" wordmark sits within reach of the mark. Set the name directly under the mark.
[check 6] At 360px the page is 366px wide, 6px of horizontal scroll. Find the element wider than the column (a fixed width, a nowrap line, desktop-size type) and fit it to 360px.

1. **Judgment 4: the list is outside the first fold at both widths.** At 1440 the 900px fold ends on the green band's "The opportunity of tomorrow" label, and no project title appears, so the declared `hero_object: list` is entirely below the fold. Pull the index up so the dougmar.ch row (title at 5xl) sits fully inside 900px; the 46vh standfirst band plus the nav sentence and the empty band header are pushing it out. At 360 the first title also starts in fold 2. Fold 1 matches `first_fold` as declared, but tighten it so the first index row at least begins in fold 1.

2. **Judgment 3: the quote leads instead of the list.** The 50px italic quote is the only large type on the desktop screen, so the phrase outranks the object it is meant to sit one step under. The small-caps project titles must be the dominant type that the eye lands on first, with the quote reading as the standfirst above them.

3. **Judgment 5: the project descriptors contradict the records.**
   - "FishSticks · SaaS · scheduling for small teams": the record says a spelling-practice tool for kids that imports school word lists.
   - "TeeTurn · tee-time swaps": the record says real-time tracking of a round's progress, with Doug responsible for product direction and strategy.
   - "Twittertale · collaborative storytelling": the record says it scanned public tweets for swear words and ranked the worst offenders.
   - "15th Club · on-course decision engine": the record says a platform for AI experiments through golf, with the scorecard as the first experiment.
   - "Politweets · political sentiment on Twitter": the record says real-time presidential-candidate mentions.

   Rewrite each from the record.

4. **Judgment 5: the Spaceman and dougmar.ch copy is wrong.**
   - The Spaceman copy ("Founding a company means fighting a hundred small systems… collapsed incorporation, cap table and first hires into a single operating surface") is invented. The record describes Spaceman as Doug's LLC for independent de

[check 5] Legibility: At 360px, <main > section.standfirst > p.nav-sentence> "Below is the evidence — see the , read t" at 16px over div.rule-layer (positioned background-image): #656b54 is under 4.5:1 across 100% of one pixel row through its glyphs (4.36:1 on #e2e6d7). Give the text a flat ground that clears the ratio (a background on its own box), or stop the lines, image or layer behind it short of the text.

1. (Judgment 1) Tonight reads as a rerun of 2026-10-05, "a founder's specimen ledger, the quote stamped over the evidence." It repeats the irregular-twelve / vertical / broken / measured / interrupted / none / balanced / reorder spine, the small-caps / italic / left / type-as-texture register, ruled ground material, and a quote set over a project index. The page even says "Below is the evidence." Keep the list as hero but change the silhouette: for example, run the index as one oversized type-as-texture field with the quote set into it rather than as a band above it, or break the strict left-aligned ruled stack. Then rewrite the "evidence" line so it does not echo that night.

2. (Judgment 5) Twittertale's line, "Experiment · ranked the worst tweets," contradicts the record. The record says it scanned public tweets for swear words and ranked which users had the biggest potty mouth. Rewrite it as something like "ranked the biggest potty mouths."

3. (Judgment 5) The dougmar.ch deck says the site is "measured against its own floors before it ships." The record says each design is scored against the previous seven builds and judged by two critics. Use the record's terms.

4. (Judgment 2) "THE OPPORTUNITY OF TOMORROW" is tiny light-green tracked caps on the dark green band, at the top of the band at 1440 and at the end of fold 1 at 360. It is barely readable. Raise its size or contrast, or drop it.

5. (Judgment 3) The visible "STANDFIRST" label above the quote is pipeline vocabulary showing as page copy, and it adds a competing label above the line. Remove it.

1. **Judgment 4: lead not fully in the phone's first fold.** At 360, fold 1 ends on the "01" label. The DOUGMAR.CH title, which is the list's lead, is cut by the fold and finishes at the top of fold 2. Tighten the space under the mark, the quote panel padding and the nav box so the first project title lands whole in fold 1 under the nav sentence. The 1440 placement passes.

2. **Judgment 1: rerun of 2026-10-05.** That night was "a founder's specimen ledger, the quote stamped over the evidence," and tonight repeats it closely:
   - the same structural spine (irregular-twelve, vertical, broken, interrupted, none, balanced, reorder)
   - the same type register (small-caps, italic lead, left, type-as-texture)
   - the same rule ground material
   - the same idea of a quote over a work ledger

   Change at least the silhouette or the type register so a returning visitor can't mistake this for that night. A forward/backward hero that echoes 10-02's "You can't go forward and backwards at the same time" makes the repetition worse.

3. **Judgment 5: Spaceman copy contradicts the records.** "The studio behind the rest of this index" claims Spaceman (2018) is behind every project, including Politweets and Twittertale from 2008, and none of the other records attribute their projects to Spaceman. Restate it from the record, for example "the LLC Doug has operated under for independent design and engineering work since 2018."

4. **Judgment 2: dougmar.ch deck at 1440.** The deck under DOUGMAR.CH is crammed into a roughly two-column green strip that breaks to one or two words per line ("This / portfolio, / redrawn…"). That makes it hard to read and leaves the row to its right empty. Give the deck a readable measure; the brief asks for this row to break wide, spanning 1–11 offset right as the caesura, not to collapse narrow.
